svg.title: The fly connectome's head-direction ring, simulated alone with fitted gains: a bump of activity in the ellipsoid body holds a heading with no cue and drifts slowly, like a fly's in darkness
svg.text: The connectome's compass holds a heading, with no cue
the head-direction ring alone (460 neurons, fitted class gains); not yet inside the whole brain
16 wedges, lit by their EPGs' spikes (100 ms frames, lightly smoothed)
The same run over a minute: where the bump sits
It drifts slowly, like a fly's in darkness: D = 0.011 rad²/s (flies: about 0.003–0.04),
and on unseen seeds of 300 s passes rung 4's bump test, visiting every wedge.
